entries.title: Sharpness gives a separate exponential rate for each subcritical parameter
entries.statement: For nearest-neighbour independent Bernoulli bond percolation on Z^d, integer d>=2, Duminil-Copin and Tassion's Theorem 1.1 states that for each fixed p<p_c there exists c(p)>0 such that P_p(0 connects to the boundary of [-n,n]^d)<=exp(-c(p)n) for all n>=1. The quantifiers do not supply a rate bounded away from zero uniformly as p increases to p_c and do not give an upper one-arm bound at p=p_c. A proof requiring critical decay needs another argument.
assumptions: Independent nearest-neighbour Bernoulli bond percolation on Z^d
Each p is fixed strictly below its critical parameter

entries.title: C0023 bond scope and Cerf's site-percolation scope differ
entries.statement: C0023 here asks whether theta_d(p_c)=0 for independent nearest-neighbour BOND percolation on Z^d, integers 3<=d<=10, with Bernoulli variables on edges. Cerf's arXiv:2608.23661 explicitly formulates theta(p_c,Z^d)=0 for independent SITE percolation, with Bernoulli variables on vertices. The product spaces and their critical parameters differ. The 2026-09-10 intake assertion that Cerf's tail conjecture is a reformulation of C0023 is not supported by the cited source alone; a model-transfer theorem would be needed to identify the tasks.
assumptions: The C0023 research lane is scoped to nearest-neighbour bond percolation
Cerf's source uses Bernoulli site percolation

relations.rationale: The existing sharpness card's phrase 'right up to p_c' needs the source's exact c(p) quantifier; both describe the same subcritical theorem.
The source theorem covers fixed p<p_c while C0023 asks for theta(p_c)=0, so it does not close the endpoint.
The target card concerns lattice criticality, while this scope check prevents merging a site-percolation tail conjecture into the bond target without a transfer proof.
